text:
Sam Patel: heads up — we just saw a burst of 5xx and client timeouts hitting hosted inference in us-west-2 starting ~11:12 UTC. errors spiked from 0.1% to ~8% over 7m. customers are starting to complain in support. opening a thread to coordinate war-room and a postmortem follow-up.

Jordan SRE: on it. I can join voice if needed. do we have a quick mitigation?

Maria Gomez: I’m seeing a large number of gateway 502/504 coming from edge-internal -> router pool. TLDR from logs: upstreams returning EOF and connection resets.

Alex Chen: I pushed an alert to #eng-sre. adding observability graphs: CPU on gateway nodes is normal, but connection pool exhaustion metrics jumped.

Tim O'Neill: can we confirm if this aligns with a deploy around 11:10? deploy-bot what’s recent? ops-bot:deploy-info

ops-bot: deploy 2026-04-18T11:05Z: router-config v2.18 rolled to us-west-2 (canary -> 100%). No rollback.

Jordan SRE: ok that’s suspicious. temporary mitigation: I’m going to scale router pool + increase max-conns to backend for next 10m. rolling now.

Sam Patel: do it. support-bot: please flag high severity and paste affected customer list.

support-bot: flagged SEV2. Affected customers (sample): Acme.ai, NoteFlow, Learnbot. Incident tickets created: INC-54321, INC-54322.

Maria Gomez: adding logs snippet — lots of this pattern from router logs: 
```
2026-04-18T11:12:34.123Z router[xyz] upstream EOF: conn-reset nid=0x7f23c error=104
2026-04-18T11:12:34.125Z router[xyz] proxy write timeout to backend id=ml-obs-03
```

Alex Chen: scaling changes are applied. initial 5xx rate down from 8% -> 3.2% in 4m. not fully recovered.

Jordan SRE: I'm attaching a reproducible curl that hits the gateway and shows intermittent 502s when run in a tight loop. can anyone run from a host in us-west-2?

Jordan SRE: ```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPO_KEY" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/models/gptx/generate" -d '{"input":"test"}'; sleep 0.2; done
```

Nina Park: ran curl from a proxy host, I got 502s ~1/8 calls, matching the spike. collected tcpdump — seeing FIN from router immediately after backend SYN-ACK in some flows.

Tim O'Neill: sounds like the router is tearing idle connections prematurely or hitting a bad code path introduced in v2.18. any config flags touched in that deploy?

Alex Chen: v2.18 included the new keepalive pool refactor and a default connection timeout tweak (15s -> 6s) to free idle conns. that could explain earlier tears.

Maria Gomez: agree. the change to aggressive idle timeout + our backend response patterns would cause mid-request resets for long tail model responses.

Sam Patel: action — rollback router-config v2.18 in us-west-2 to previous stable. Jordan, can you coordinate?

Jordan SRE: rolling back now to v2.17. watch logs for ~5m. status: rollback started.

ops-bot: rollback initiated by Jordan SRE at 11:23:10Z, target us-west-2.

Jordan SRE: rollback complete at 11:27Z. 5xx dropped to baseline <0.3% within ~3m.

Sam Patel: good. capturing timeline for postmortem. immediate mitigation = rollback. next steps we should track here: repro, root cause, test coverage, long-term fix, customer outreach.

Maria Gomez: root cause (hypothesis) = keepalive/idle-timeout refactor + aggressive default timeout (6s) causing in-flight model responses to be cut. reproduced consistently with curl.

Alex Chen: risk: v2.18 also added a pooling refactor that changes conn reuse. need unit + integration tests for long-running backend responses and a canary plan that simulates model latency tail.

Nina Park: adding repro steps I used: run the curl loop from within us-west-2, or use loadgen with 50 concurrent clients, model response latency artificially delayed 8-12s (we used a test backend that sleeps). observed ~12% failure if idle-timeout <=6s.

Jordan SRE: mitigation checklist completed: rollback, scale bump, customer tickets opened, monitoring dashboard annotated.

Sam Patel: assigning action items: 1) Alex — add regression test for keepalive refactor (owner: Alex Chen, due: 2026-04-25). 2) Tim — review and harden default timeouts + config flags + make aggressive defaults opt-in (owner: Tim O'Neill, due: 2026-04-22). 3) Maria — run a canary job that simulates model tail latencies across deployments for 72h (owner: Maria Gomez, due: 2026-04-24). 4) Jordan — write postmortem draft with timeline, RCA, mitigation and link to rollbacks + tickets (owner: Jordan SRE, due: 2026-04-20). 5) Nina — attach tcpdumps and repro artifacts to INC tickets (owner: Nina Park, due: 2026-04-19).

Sam Patel: Nina, please prepare a short customer-safe summary we can paste into INC tickets and support threads. Sam will take point on support comms.

Nina Park: will do, drafting now.

Alex Chen: quick note for deploy process: add a preflight that runs a 90s model-latency simulation against any router config change during canary phase. small harness should catch this.

Tim O'Neill: +1. also propose adding a feature flag gate for aggressive idle-timeout so it doesn't auto-roll to 100% until validated by canary metrics.

Jordan SRE: tagging this conversation for postmortem: link (internal) will be posted in the next 24h.

support-bot: customers notified via INC tickets. status: mitigation complete, awaiting PM follow-up.

Sam Patel: thanks everyone. lessons learned: don't tighten idle timeouts without simulating model tail; ensure connection pooling refactor has integration testing for long-lived responses; improve deploy canary checks. I’ll close the warroom once postmortem is up and action owners acknowledged. :white_check_mark:

Jordan SRE: ack, will start the postmortem draft now.

Maria Gomez: ack. adding test cases to CI board.

Alex Chen: ack. creating a PR template item for long-tail latency tests.

Tim O'Neill: ack, will update default config and add opt-in flag.

Nina Park: will upload artifacts by EOD.

Sam Patel: last entry: if anyone sees residual customer errors, ping me directly. closing thread in ~24h after postmortem link posted. :lock:
